title: Best Beaches & Beachfront Stays in Brijuni, Croatia 2027
metaDescription: Brijuni beaches and seafront stays: Saluga beach, Veliki Brijun hotels and apartments, 2027 ticket prices in euros, boat access from Fažana and tips.
content:
## Best Beaches in Brijuni

Brijuni National Park has 14 islands and 12 islets, but visitors can reach only Veliki Brijun and Mali Brijun. Beaches here are rocky or pebbled, with pine shade right behind the shoreline. They are not sandy resort beaches. Anyone expecting sand should look at the mainland coast around Fažana instead.

### Saluga Beach, Veliki Brijun

Saluga is the main swimming spot and the one hotel guests use. It sits about 500–600 m from the port and the Hotel Istra and Neptun area, a walk of under 10 minutes. The shore is rocky and pebbled, so water shoes are useful. Sunbeds are available nearby, and hotel guests have been charged a reduced rate of around €5 per day.

### Rocky coves along the island's coast

Veliki Brijun has a long, indented coastline with many small rocky coves and flat rock platforms used for swimming. Reaching them takes a bike or a walk along the park paths. Swimming outside designated areas is allowed in most places, but the park's rules on nature protection apply, and no lifeguards are present.

### Boat-tour swim stops

Boat tours from Fažana and Pula add swim and snorkel stops in bays around the archipelago, including areas that day visitors on the standard ticket never reach. Prices for these tours start around €25–30 per person, with lunch and drinks packages costing more.

> **Opinion:** Day visitors overrate the beach side of Brijuni. A standard visit is built around the Safari Park, the Roman remains and the tourist train, and there is little time left to swim. Anyone who mainly wants a beach day will get better value from a swim-and-snorkel boat tour or a mainland Istrian beach.

## Beachfront Apartments in Brijuni: What Exists

Independent holiday rentals do not exist on the islands. All accommodation is run by the national park, which means no private apartment listings. The seafront options are on Veliki Brijun, around the main port.

### Hotel Istra and Hotel Neptun annex

Hotel Istra has 32 double rooms over three floors, on the seafront in the main port. Sea-view rooms face the port, the Fažana Channel and the Istrian mainland. The Neptun annex is in the same port, in Austro-Hungarian style, and offers rooms and sea-facing apartments. Per-person prices with breakfast in 2026 ran from about €62 for a standard park-view double at Istra up to about €145 for a superior room in peak summer. Neptun apartments ran from about €61 to €94 per person.

### Rooms Karmen

Karmen is a simple 2★ property with 53 rooms on three floors, by the sea near the Neptun-Istra complex. Rooms have no minibar, and there is one sea-side apartment. It is the cheapest official option.

### Luxury villas

The park also rents out Villa Dubravka, Villa Lovorka and Villa Primorka. Prices are quoted on request.

### What the price includes

- Breakfast (dinner is an optional extra, usually a buffet)
- Boat transfer from Fažana, one crossing per day on the park's regular line
- National park entry and insurance
- A discount of around 15–20% on park programmes for hotel guests

A stay of at least 3 nights is typically required for the apartments. Pets are not allowed in most units. Bicycles cannot be brought to the island, but they can be hired there.

## How to Get to Brijuni

The only access is the park's boat from Fažana, a crossing of about 15 minutes. Fažana is roughly 8 km from Pula. Guarded parking in Fažana cost €12 per vehicle per day in 2026, rising to €15 in June, July, August and September.

## Ticket Prices

| Ticket | Oct–May | Jun–Sep |
|---|---|---|
| Self-guided, adult | €30 | €40 |
| Guided with train, adult | €35 | €50 |
| Child 7–18, guided | €15 | €20 |
| Evening entry (Jul–Aug) | – | €15 |

Children under 7 go free, and a dog ticket costs €15. Dogs cannot enter the Safari Park, the train or the museums. Individual visits are not possible in January and February.

## Insider Tips

- The €15 evening ticket (departures at 18:00, 19:00 and 20:00 in high season) is the cheapest way to swim at Saluga and eat dinner on the island, though it skips the main sights.
- Book July and August weekends well ahead, since boat capacity is limited.
- Bring water shoes and a mask. The coast is rocky, and the water is clear.
- A stay of 2–3 nights lets visitors swim in the early morning, before day-trip boats arrive.
- Hotel guests walk only a few steps from the port to the hotel entrance, so luggage is easy.

## Best Time to Visit

Sea temperatures suit swimming from June to September. May and October are quieter and cheaper, with a €30 self-guided ticket, but the water is cooler.

faq.question: What is the best beach in Brijuni?
faq.answer: Saluga on Veliki Brijun is the main beach, about 500–600 m from the port. It is rocky and pebbled, with sunbeds nearby and pine shade.

faq.question: Are there beachfront apartments in Brijuni?
faq.answer: Only park-run seafront options exist: the Neptun annex apartments, Hotel Istra, Rooms Karmen and three luxury villas. Private rentals are not available on the islands. Fažana on the mainland has independent apartments.

faq.question: How much does it cost to stay in Brijuni?
faq.answer: In 2026, per-person prices with breakfast ran from about €61 for a Neptun apartment to about €145 for a superior Istra room in peak season. The price includes the Fažana boat and park entry. A minimum of 3 nights often applies.

faq.question: How do you get to Brijuni?
faq.answer: Take the national park's boat from Fažana, a crossing of about 15 minutes. Private boats cannot land without permission. Parking in Fažana costs €12–15 per day.

faq.question: How much is a Brijuni day ticket?
faq.answer: A self-guided adult ticket costs €40 from June to September and €30 from October to May. The guided ticket with the tourist train costs €50 in summer and €35 off-season. Children under 7 enter free.

faq.question: Can you swim at Brijuni on a day trip?
faq.answer: Yes, at Saluga beach and from rocky coves, but the standard day program leaves limited time. Swim-and-snorkel boat tours include dedicated swimming stops.

quickAnswer: Brijuni's most accessible beach is Saluga on Veliki Brijun, about 500–600 m from the main port. Seafront apartments are limited to park-run properties: Hotel Istra, Hotel Neptun and Rooms Karmen, at roughly €61–145 per person per night with breakfast. All stays include the Fažana boat and park ticket.
